conversation.text: I'd hold the first number as the answer so far, then walk the rest of the list once and swap in any number that beats it.
As you move along, how much of what you've already seen do you actually still need?
Just the one biggest value I'm holding. I don't need to remember anything else I've passed. When the list runs out, whatever I'm holding is the answer. That's O(n) time and O(1) space.
I'd sort the whole list ascending, then return the last element.
Sorting puts every number in its place. Do you need all of them in place to answer this, or only one of them?
Only the biggest one, really. But sorting is simple to reason about, so I'd still do that -- it's O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
I'd just return the first element of the list.
What does your answer give for [3, 9, 2, 7], and is that the number the question asked for?
It gives 3. I think that's fine since the list should already be roughly in order by the time it gets to me.
I'd probably just write a SQL query for this, something with GROUP BY.
